subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw core standardize a markdown per-skill preference sidecar, use structured `skills.entries` config for this need, or keep the current full-`SKILL.md` override model?
rationale: The requested behavior changes the model-facing skill contract, skill-source precedence, prompt-version semantics, and user configuration surface, so automation should not pick the permanent API shape.

options.title: Approve a markdown sidecar contract
options.body: Standardize a narrow `preferences.md`-style file with lower precedence than `SKILL.md`, explicit version/watcher semantics, docs, and tests.

options.title: Use structured skill config only
options.body: Extend or document `skills.entries.<key>.config` for machine-readable preferences, accepting that natural-language conventions remain less ergonomic.

options.title: Keep override-only behavior
options.body: Leave preferences in full `SKILL.md` overrides or global context files and close this direction as outside the current core scope.

recommendation.title: Approve a markdown sidecar contract
recommendation.body: Standardize a narrow `preferences.md`-style file with lower precedence than `SKILL.md`, explicit version/watcher semantics, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest historical signal on skill config, skill invocation, ClawHub install flows, and skill path containment decisions.
